title: Subtenon Vs Intravitreal Triamcinolone injection in Diabetic Macular Edema, A prospective study in Chinese population

license.statement: CC BY 3.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/)

condition: Diabetic macular edema (type 1 or 2 diabetes) with macular thickening on OCT, phakic eyes without vitreoretinal traction, previously treated with laser photocoagulation; prospective paired-eye study in which one eye received intravitreal and the fellow eye sub-Tenon triamcinolone (20 patients, 40 eyes; Shanghai First People's Hospital, 2011-2013); 12-week follow-up

groups.agent: intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide, single injection (30-gauge needle; dose not stated in the Methods)
sub-Tenon triamcinolone acetonide, single injection (27-gauge needle, placement checked by B-scan; dose not stated in the Methods)
groups.description: Fellow eye of the same patients, injected one week after the intravitreal eye

series.baseline_label: Baseline (Table II, row 2, IVTA column; before injection)
series.notes: mean ± SD (Table II footnote); scheduled visits 2, 4, 8 and 12 weeks after the injection (weeks x 7 / 30.4375 months); per-visit n not reported

series.baseline_label: Baseline (Table II, row 2, SBTA column; before injection)
series.notes: mean ± SD (Table II footnote); scheduled visits 2, 4, 8 and 12 weeks after the injection of this eye (weeks x 7 / 30.4375 months); per-visit n not reported

notes: CMT was measured by OCT with six radial scans per eye; the OCT device and the CMT definition are not stated.
The two series are fellow eyes of the same 20 patients (paired design), not the same eyes.
Visual acuity and IOP are reported (not extracted).
Ambiguity resolved: the study tests sub-Tenon triamcinolone as an alternative route to intravitreal triamcinolone without an investigational agent, so both groups are control.
Ambiguity resolved: inclusion required previous laser photocoagulation, so prior_treatment is previously_treated.
